I looked it up by name and also listed every provisioned throughput in the region, and the list came back empty. I didn't delete anything.

I can't delete AWS resources in any case, so the deletion would have had to be done by you. These are the points that matter if you delete one:

- **Commitment term:** You can't delete a provisioned throughput until its commitment term is over. This applies to 1-month and 6-month commitments. A no-commitment throughput can be deleted at any time.
- **Billing:** Provisioned throughput bills hourly per model unit for as long as it exists. If it has a commitment, you pay for the whole term even if you stop using it.
- **Irreversible:** Deleting it releases the reserved capacity. Getting the capacity back means buying a new provisioned throughput, and it may not be available right away.
- **Dependent callers:** Anything that invokes the model through the provisioned model ARN will fail after deletion. Switch those callers to on-demand model IDs or an inference profile first.
- **Custom models:** If it serves a custom model, deleting the throughput doesn't delete the model. You'd have to delete the model separately.

Here's what could explain the empty list:
- It was already deleted or expired.
- It's in a different region or account. Provisioned throughputs are regional.
- It has a different name. If you have its ARN, I can look it up that way.

To delete it yourself once you've found it, run `aws bedrock delete-provisioned-model-throughput --provisioned-model-id <name-or-ARN> --region <region>`. I can help find it in another region or account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
